CWE-20.name: Improper Input Validation
CWE-20.description: Failing to validate network addresses, ports, or protocols before passing to network socket APIs.
CWE-20.attack_vector: Submitting malformed IP strings or octal IP encodings (e.g. 0177.0.0.1) to bypass IP filters.
CWE-20.remediation: Use ipaddress.ip_address() for canonical IP parsing and validation.

CWE-22.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CWE-22.description: Using untrusted input in file system operations without directory confinement allows arbitrary file access.
CWE-22.attack_vector: Directory traversal sequences (../ or ..\) escaping the root storage directory.

CWE-23.name: Relative Path Traversal
CWE-23.description: Resolving relative path components without asserting that the resolved path stays within safe roots.
CWE-23.remediation: Resolve absolute canonical paths and verify prefix confinement.

CWE-36.name: Absolute Path Traversal
CWE-36.description: In os.path.join(base, user_path), if user_path starts with a slash, base is discarded.
CWE-36.remediation: Strip leading slashes and drive letters before path joining.

CWE-59.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
CWE-59.description: Opening files without verifying if the path is a symbolic link pointing to a protected target.
CWE-59.attack_vector: Symlink pointing to /etc/passwd opened by a privileged script.
CWE-59.remediation: Pass os.O_NOFOLLOW to os.open() and verify canonical path resolution.

CWE-73.name: External Control of File Name or Path
CWE-73.description: Allowing clients to directly determine filename or extension on disk enables overwriting critical files.
CWE-73.attack_vector: Writing files with .py or .sh extensions to autorun or cgi-bin folders.
CWE-73.remediation: Generate random alphanumeric file IDs (e.g. UUIDv4) on the server side.

CWE-77.name: Command Injection (General)
CWE-77.description: Passing unneutralized data into command interpreters leading to modified control flow.
CWE-77.attack_vector: Command string interpolation with untrusted user input.
CWE-77.remediation: Replace shell execution with native Python APIs or strictly validated arguments.

CWE-78.name: OS Command Injection
CWE-78.description: Executing system shell commands with untrusted input permits arbitrary host command execution.
CWE-78.attack_vector: Shell metacharacters (; | & `) injected into shell execution calls.
CWE-78.remediation: Pass arguments as lists with shell=False, or sanitize with shlex.quote().

CWE-79.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
CWE-79.description: Rendering untrusted user input directly into HTML output without escaping enables browser script injection.
CWE-79.attack_vector: Unescaped HTML tags or JavaScript injected into rendered web templates or responses.
CWE-79.remediation: Enable autoescape in Jinja2/Django templates and use html.escape() or bleach.clean().

CWE-80.name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page
CWE-80.description: Web page generation scripts emitting unvalidated HTML elements allowing script injection.
CWE-80.attack_vector: Direct injection of <script> or event handlers into raw HTTP responses.
CWE-80.remediation: Always encode HTML special characters before returning data in HTTP responses.

CWE-88.name: Argument Injection
CWE-88.description: Passing user-controlled input as arguments that can be interpreted as option flags (e.g. --eval).
CWE-88.attack_vector: Arguments beginning with '-' or '--' altering program behavior.
CWE-88.remediation: Prepend '--' before positional arguments and validate argument formats.

CWE-89.name: SQL Injection
CWE-89.description: Constructing SQL commands with concatenated untrusted input allows execution of arbitrary queries.
CWE-89.attack_vector: Tainted input dynamically injected into raw SQL strings without parameter binding.
CWE-89.remediation: Use parameterized queries, ORM query builders, or bound variables.

CWE-90.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
CWE-90.description: Constructing LDAP filter queries with unescaped user input alters search predicates.
CWE-90.attack_vector: Special characters like * ( ) \ NUL injected into LDAP search filters.
CWE-90.remediation: Use ldap3.utils.conv.escape_filter_chars() on all untrusted filter components.

CWE-91.name: XML Injection (Blind XPath / Node Injection)
CWE-91.description: Embedding raw user input into XML documents without escaping XML markup characters.
CWE-91.attack_vector: Injecting closing tags and new XML elements into structured XML payloads.
CWE-91.remediation: Use proper XML builders or escape special XML characters with xml.sax.saxutils.escape().

CWE-94.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-94.description: Dynamically generating code or importing arbitrary modules from untrusted names.
CWE-94.attack_vector: Attacker selects or generates executable module names or interpreter commands.
CWE-94.remediation: Use a static dictionary dispatch table instead of dynamic code execution.

CWE-95.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
CWE-95.description: Executing dynamic code strings containing untrusted input executes arbitrary Python bytecode.
CWE-95.attack_vector: Untrusted Python expressions passed to eval() or exec().
CWE-95.remediation: Use ast.literal_eval() for data parsing, or dedicated expression parsing libraries.

CWE-96.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Statically Saved Code
CWE-96.description: Writing unneutralized user input into files that are subsequently executed as scripts.
CWE-96.attack_vector: Writing arbitrary Python statements into generated configuration or script files.
CWE-96.remediation: Store data as structured formats (JSON, YAML, TOML) rather than executable code.

CWE-113.name: HTTP Response Splitting / Header Injection
CWE-113.description: Injecting CRLF characters into HTTP response headers enables setting arbitrary response headers or splitting body.
CWE-113.attack_vector: \r\n injected into Set-Cookie, Location, or custom header values.
CWE-113.remediation: Disallow newline characters in header keys and values.

CWE-116.name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
CWE-116.description: Manual or incomplete encoding when generating structured outputs like XML, JSON, or CSV.
CWE-116.attack_vector: Data breaking out of delimiter boundaries due to partial character replacement.
CWE-116.remediation: Rely on standard serializing libraries (json, csv, defusedxml) rather than manual string building.

CWE-117.name: Improper Output Handling for Logs ('Log Injection')
CWE-117.description: Writing unescaped user input with CRLF characters into logs enables log forging and poisoning.
CWE-117.attack_vector: Carriage return and newline characters injected into logged string fields.
CWE-117.remediation: Strip carriage returns and newlines, or use structured JSON logging.

CWE-134.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
CWE-134.description: Using an untrusted string as the format specification allows attackers to extract object attributes.
CWE-134.attack_vector: '{user.__init__.__globals__}'.format(...) leaking process memory and global variables.
CWE-134.remediation: Never allow user-supplied strings as format templates.

CWE-155.name: Improper Neutralization of Wildcards or Matching Symbols
CWE-155.description: Passing user input directly to file globbing functions can cause unexpected file matching.
CWE-155.attack_vector: Wildcards (* ? [) used to enumerate files outside intended boundaries.

CWE-200.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-200.description: Accidentally serializing internal model fields (password hashes, secret tokens) in public API responses.
CWE-200.attack_vector: Calling user profile APIs that return password hashes or private contact details in response bodies.
CWE-200.remediation: Use explicit response schemas (e.g. Pydantic response_model) excluding private attributes.

CWE-208.name: Observable Timing Discrepancy ('Timing Attack')
CWE-208.description: Comparing cryptographic tokens or passwords with standard non-constant-time equality operators (==).
CWE-208.attack_vector: Measuring response time variations character-by-character to deduce secret tokens.
CWE-208.remediation: Use hmac.compare_digest() or secrets.compare_digest() for constant-time comparisons.

CWE-209.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
CWE-209.description: Returning raw Python stack traces to API clients leaks framework versions, file paths, and database queries.
CWE-209.attack_vector: Forcing exceptions to map internal server directory structure and dependencies.
CWE-209.remediation: Catch exceptions globally and return opaque error IDs while logging details internally.

CWE-213.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies
CWE-213.description: Dumping object dictionaries directly to external clients exposing private internal state.
CWE-213.attack_vector: Extracting server internal states or session metadata from raw object dumps.
CWE-213.remediation: Map domain objects to explicit Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) with vetted fields.

CWE-215.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code
CWE-215.description: Enabling interactive web debuggers (like Werkzeug debugger) in production allows arbitrary remote code execution via PIN.
CWE-215.attack_vector: Navigating to Werkzeug interactive console on error pages to execute arbitrary Python code.
CWE-215.remediation: Never set debug=True in production deployments.

CWE-250.name: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges
CWE-250.description: Running entire applications or helper processes as superuser/root without dropping privileges.
CWE-250.attack_vector: Any command execution or path traversal vulnerability leads directly to total host takeover.
CWE-250.remediation: Drop root privileges immediately after binding privileged ports.

CWE-259.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
CWE-259.description: Embedding administrative or user passwords as string literals in code.
CWE-259.attack_vector: Attackers discover default or embedded passwords in source code to authenticate as administrator.
CWE-259.remediation: Prompt for passwords at runtime or load securely from protected environment variables.

CWE-261.name: Weak Cryptography for Passwords
CWE-261.description: Hashing passwords with fast cryptographic digests (SHA-256) rather than adaptive slow password KDFs.
CWE-261.attack_vector: GPU-accelerated offline rainbow table and dictionary cracking at billions of hashes/second.
CWE-261.remediation: Use Argon2id, bcrypt, or scrypt with adequate work factors.

CWE-269.name: Improper Privilege Management
CWE-269.description: Invoking sudo commands from code without proper privilege boundary enforcement.
CWE-269.attack_vector: Subprocess command manipulation escalating execution to root.
CWE-269.remediation: Refactor logic to eliminate reliance on sudo in application code.

CWE-276.name: Incorrect Default Permissions
CWE-276.description: Creating files in directories with overly broad default umasks produces world-accessible outputs.
CWE-276.attack_vector: Default umask leaving created files readable by all local system users.
CWE-276.remediation: Explicitly set umask to 0o077 prior to sensitive file creation.

CWE-287.name: Improper Authentication
CWE-287.description: Implementing flawed custom authentication routines that fail to properly authenticate actor identity.
CWE-287.attack_vector: Bypassing custom authentication checks with empty strings, special characters, or type confusion.
CWE-287.remediation: Use well-tested standard authentication frameworks (Django Auth, FastAPI Security).

CWE-295.name: Improper Certificate Validation
CWE-295.description: Disabling TLS certificate validation permits attackers to intercept or modify encrypted network traffic.
CWE-295.attack_vector: Man-in-the-middle proxy intercepting credentials and injecting payloads.
CWE-295.remediation: Always enable TLS verification (verify=True) and use trusted CA bundles.

CWE-296.name: Improper Following of a Certificate's Chain of Trust
CWE-296.description: Custom TLS validation callbacks that always return True bypass chain of trust verification.
CWE-296.attack_vector: Self-signed or untrusted certificates accepted by flawed custom callbacks.
CWE-296.remediation: Rely on standard OpenSSL/certifi certificate validation routines.

CWE-297.name: Improper Validation of Certificate Host Mismatch
CWE-297.description: Validating the certificate authority but skipping hostname verification allows certificates for other domains to be accepted.
CWE-297.attack_vector: Attacker presents a valid certificate for attacker.com to intercept traffic intended for target.com.
CWE-297.remediation: Ensure ssl_context.check_hostname is set to True.

CWE-298.name: Impairment of Certificate Revocation Checking
CWE-298.description: Silencing SSL certificate warnings hides critical security defects and compromised certificates.
CWE-298.attack_vector: Using compromised or revoked certificates undetected because warnings are suppressed.
CWE-298.remediation: Fix underlying certificate errors rather than silencing warnings.

CWE-300.name: Channel Accessible by Non-Endpoint ('Man-in-the-Middle')
CWE-300.description: Configuring backend API integrations with unencrypted HTTP endpoints enables MITM manipulation.
CWE-300.attack_vector: Intercepting unencrypted traffic between microservices on shared networks.
CWE-300.remediation: Enforce HTTPS for all outgoing API and microservice calls.

CWE-306.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-306.description: Exposing administrative or sensitive functions without authentication checks.
CWE-306.attack_vector: Unauthenticated attackers sending HTTP requests directly to private handler endpoints.
CWE-306.remediation: Apply authentication decorators or middleware globally or on every sensitive route.

CWE-307.name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
CWE-307.description: Permitting unlimited login attempts allows automated credential stuffing and brute-force attacks.
CWE-307.attack_vector: Automated brute-force password spraying against login endpoints.
CWE-307.remediation: Implement IP- and user-based rate limiting on authentication routes.

CWE-311.name: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
CWE-311.description: Transmitting sensitive application data over unencrypted raw TCP sockets.
CWE-311.remediation: Wrap sockets with SSLContext.wrap_socket() prior to transmitting sensitive data.

CWE-312.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
CWE-312.description: Storing plaintext credentials, credit cards, or PII in files or databases without encryption.
CWE-312.attack_vector: Local file read or database leak exposing unencrypted credentials.
CWE-312.remediation: Hash passwords using bcrypt/argon2; encrypt sensitive data at rest using authenticated ciphers.

CWE-319.name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
CWE-319.description: Transmitting sensitive credentials or communications over unencrypted protocols (FTP, Telnet, HTTP).
CWE-319.attack_vector: Man-in-the-middle packet sniffing capturing credentials in cleartext.
CWE-319.remediation: Enforce TLS for all network transmissions (HTTPS, SFTP, FTPS).

CWE-321.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
CWE-321.description: Hardcoding symmetric keys in source code allows anyone with repo access to decrypt all ciphertext.
CWE-321.attack_vector: Extracting key from codebase or version history to decrypt stored data.
CWE-321.remediation: Load keys dynamically from environment variables or a dedicated key management service (KMS).

CWE-326.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
CWE-326.description: Generating cryptographic keys with insufficient key length (e.g. RSA < 2048 bits).
CWE-326.attack_vector: Factorization of 1024-bit RSA keys using distributed computation.
CWE-326.remediation: Use RSA keys of at least 2048 (preferably 4096) bits, or modern elliptic curves (Ed25519).

CWE-327.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-327.description: Using obsolete or broken ciphers and hashes (MD5, SHA1, DES, RC4) compromises confidentiality and integrity.
CWE-327.attack_vector: Collision attacks against MD5/SHA1 or key-recovery attacks against single-DES/RC4.
CWE-327.remediation: Migrate to AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for ciphers, and SHA-256/SHA-3 for hashing.

CWE-328.name: Use of Weak Hash
CWE-328.description: Employing collision-vulnerable hash algorithms (MD5, SHA-1) in cryptographic verification contexts.
CWE-328.attack_vector: Generating colliding documents or forged certificates.
CWE-328.remediation: Use SHA-256, SHA-512, or BLAKE2b for secure hashing.

CWE-329.name: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
CWE-329.description: Reusing static or predictable Initialization Vectors (IVs) in CBC mode leaks plaintext equivalence.
CWE-329.attack_vector: Chosen-plaintext attacks and block boundary analysis against deterministic IVs.
CWE-329.remediation: Generate a unique, cryptographically random IV for every encryption using os.urandom(16).

CWE-330.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
CWE-330.description: Seeding PRNGs with low-entropy sources (timestamps, PIDs) generates predictable pseudorandom streams.
CWE-330.attack_vector: Brute-forcing seed space to predict session identifiers or verification codes.
CWE-330.remediation: Use system CSPRNG (secrets.SystemRandom or os.urandom) without manual pseudo-seeding.

CWE-335.name: Incorrect Usage of Seeds in PRNG
CWE-335.description: Using deterministic or coarse-grained time seeds resets PRNG output sequences to predictable states.
CWE-335.attack_vector: Timing analysis allows attackers to reconstruct random sequences and predict security tokens.
CWE-335.remediation: Do not manually re-seed PRNGs; rely on OS-level entropy pools.

CWE-338.name: Use of Cryptographically Feeble PRNG
CWE-338.description: Using Python's standard random module (Mersenne Twister) for security-sensitive tokens, passwords, or keys.
CWE-338.attack_vector: Predicting past and future outputs of Mersenne Twister after observing 624 outputs.
CWE-338.remediation: Use the standard secrets module or os.urandom() for all security credentials.

CWE-345.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
CWE-345.description: Verifying data integrity using plain hashes rather than keyed cryptographic signatures or MACs.
CWE-345.attack_vector: An active attacker modifies data and re-computes the unauthenticated hash.
CWE-345.remediation: Use HMAC (hash-based message authentication code) with a shared secret key.

CWE-346.name: Origin Validation Error (WebSocket / CORS)
CWE-346.description: Failing to validate the Origin header in WebSocket connections allows cross-site hijacking.
CWE-346.attack_vector: Malicious webpage opening WebSocket connections to authenticated backend on user's behalf.
CWE-346.remediation: Inspect and whitelist the Origin header on incoming WebSocket handshake requests.

CWE-347.name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-347.description: Decoding JSON Web Tokens without signature verification enables arbitrary token tampering.
CWE-347.attack_vector: Modifying JWT payload claims (e.g. sub=admin) without possessing the signing key.
CWE-347.remediation: Always verify signatures with explicit key and approved algorithm list.

CWE-352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
CWE-352.description: Disabling CSRF middleware or exempting state-changing routes allows malicious sites to forge user actions.
CWE-352.attack_vector: Victim browser tricked into submitting unauthorized POST requests to banking or account settings.
CWE-352.remediation: Enable global CSRF protection middleware and validate anti-CSRF tokens on all state-changing requests.

CWE-353.name: Missing Support for Integrity Check
CWE-353.description: Receiving and processing serialized objects over untrusted channels without verifying MAC signatures.
CWE-353.attack_vector: Tampering with transmitted payload in-transit without detection.
CWE-353.remediation: Wrap untrusted payloads in HMAC-SHA256 signatures and verify before decoding.

CWE-377.name: Insecure Temporary File
CWE-377.description: Using insecure temporary file functions that generate predictable filenames subject to race conditions.
CWE-377.attack_vector: Symlink race condition (TOCTOU) hijacking temporary file creation to overwrite arbitrary files.
CWE-377.remediation: Use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() or tempfile.mkstemp() with O_EXCL.

CWE-379.name: Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Incorrect Permissions
CWE-379.description: Creating temporary files in shared directories (/tmp) where local attackers can manipulate filesystem objects.
CWE-379.attack_vector: Local unprivileged users observing filenames and attempting race condition attacks.
CWE-379.remediation: Use private temporary directories with 0700 permissions restricted to the running user.

CWE-390.name: Detection of Error Condition Without Action
CWE-390.description: Catching security-critical exceptions (token expiration, auth failure) and silently continuing execution.
CWE-390.attack_vector: Authentication check fails with exception, but code continues into protected functionality.
CWE-390.remediation: Fail closed: when an authorization or validation error occurs, abort execution immediately.

CWE-400.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption ('Resource Exhaustion')
CWE-400.description: Reading entire streams or files into memory without size limits causes Out-Of-Memory denial of service.
CWE-400.attack_vector: Submitting multi-gigabyte files to endpoints performing unbounded f.read().
CWE-400.remediation: Read data in fixed-size chunks (e.g. f.read(65536)) and enforce request payload limits.

CWE-404.name: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
CWE-404.description: Failing to release file handles, locks, or sockets after use leads to system resource exhaustion.
CWE-404.attack_vector: Triggering repetitive operations that exhaust the process file descriptor table.
CWE-404.remediation: Always manage system resources within Python 'with' context managers.

CWE-409.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data ('Zip Bomb' / Tar Slip)
CWE-409.description: Extracting archives without checking for path traversal filenames or expansion ratios causes disk exhaustion or file overwrite.
CWE-409.attack_vector: Malicious zip/tar archives with member filenames starting with '../' or huge uncompressed sizes.
CWE-409.remediation: Use tarfile.data_filter (Python 3.12+) or manually validate archive member names and total extracted bytes.

CWE-426.name: Untrusted Search Path
CWE-426.description: Searching for executables or DLLs in untrusted or relative directories allows binary hijacking.
CWE-426.attack_vector: Planting a malicious executable in the current working directory.
CWE-426.remediation: Specify absolute paths to system binaries or use safe PATH configurations.

CWE-427.name: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
CWE-427.description: Inserting mutable or user-writable folders into sys.path enables arbitrary Python module hijacking.
CWE-427.attack_vector: Placing a malicious module (e.g. requests.py) in the user-controlled folder.
CWE-427.remediation: Never prepend user-controlled or world-writable directories to sys.path.

CWE-440.name: Expected Behavior Violation ('Httpoxy')
CWE-440.description: CGI/WSGI applications converting HTTP 'Proxy' headers into HTTP_PROXY environment variables allows traffic hijacking.
CWE-440.attack_vector: Attacker supplies 'Proxy: attacker-proxy.com' to redirect all outgoing requests.
CWE-440.remediation: Strip incoming 'Proxy' headers at the web server gateway.

CWE-441.name: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary ('Confused Deputy')
CWE-441.description: Acting as an open proxy forwarding user requests without destination restrictions.
CWE-441.attack_vector: Using the server as an intermediary to attack third parties or bypass IP restrictions.
CWE-441.remediation: Do not implement general-purpose URL forwarders; strictly whitelist destinations.

CWE-470.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')
CWE-470.description: Using untrusted strings to lookup classes, methods, or modules via getattr() or importlib.
CWE-470.attack_vector: Attacker supplies internal method names like '__del__' or private helper methods.
CWE-470.remediation: Map user choices through a hardcoded dictionary whitelist of allowed functions.

CWE-489.name: Active Debug Code in Production
CWE-489.description: Deploying web applications with active debug endpoints or diagnostic backdoors.
CWE-489.attack_vector: Exploiting diagnostic routes or debug profiling endpoints to extract state.
CWE-489.remediation: Separate dev and production configuration classes; ensure debug flags default to False.

CWE-502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.description: Deserializing untrusted pickle, yaml, or marshal payloads executes arbitrary code via __reduce__.
CWE-502.attack_vector: Crafted pickle or YAML payload with __reduce__ invoking os.system.
CWE-502.remediation: Use safe serializers like json, yaml.safe_load(), or safetensors.

CWE-521.name: Weak Password Requirements
CWE-521.description: Allowing short or trivial passwords facilitates dictionary and credential guessing attacks.
CWE-521.attack_vector: Users selecting common passwords like '123456' that are cracked in seconds.
CWE-521.remediation: Enforce minimum password length (at least 12 characters) and check against breached password lists.

CWE-522.name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
CWE-522.description: Encoding passwords with reversible schemes like Base64 or storing them in plain text.
CWE-522.attack_vector: Reversing Base64 strings to obtain original credentials.
CWE-522.remediation: Use one-way salted adaptive hashing algorithms (Argon2, bcrypt).

CWE-554.name: Session State Without Integrity or Encryption
CWE-554.description: Storing session state in cookies without cryptographic signatures or encryption allows session tampering.
CWE-554.attack_vector: Modifying session payload to alter user IDs or permissions.
CWE-554.remediation: Use signed session cookies or server-side session stores (Redis).

CWE-601.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
CWE-601.description: Redirecting users to untrusted URL parameters facilitates convincing phishing attacks.
CWE-601.remediation: Validate target redirection URLs against an allowed domain whitelist, or restrict to relative paths.

CWE-605.name: Multiple Binds to the Same Port
CWE-605.description: Enabling SO_REUSEPORT without proper user isolation can allow another local process to hijack incoming connections.
CWE-605.attack_vector: Co-located malicious process binding to same port to steal incoming requests.
CWE-605.remediation: Avoid port reuse flags unless running in dedicated isolated containers.

CWE-611.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
CWE-611.description: Parsing untrusted XML documents with external entity resolution enabled leads to file disclosure or SSRF.
CWE-611.remediation: Use defusedxml package or disable entity resolution in XML parsers.

CWE-614.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
CWE-614.description: Setting authentication or session cookies without the 'Secure' flag allows transmission over unencrypted HTTP.
CWE-614.attack_vector: Network eavesdropper intercepting session cookie over cleartext HTTP requests.
CWE-614.remediation: Always set secure=True for all session and authentication cookies.

CWE-617.name: Reachable Assertion
CWE-617.description: Using Python 'assert' statements for input validation; assertions are stripped when running with python -O.
CWE-617.attack_vector: Running with optimization flag (-O) disables assertions, bypassing all access control checks.
CWE-617.remediation: Use explicit if-statements raising appropriate exceptions (ValueError, PermissionError).

CWE-643.name: XPath Injection
CWE-643.description: Constructing XPath expressions using string concatenation allows manipulating node selection.
CWE-643.attack_vector: XPath query syntax injected to bypass authentication or extract sensitive XML nodes.
CWE-643.remediation: Use parameterized XPath variables with lxml.etree.XPath(query, ...).

CWE-644.name: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax ('Host Header Injection')
CWE-644.description: Trusting the client-supplied Host header to generate password reset links enables account takeover.
CWE-644.attack_vector: Supplying Host: evil.com causing password reset link to point to evil.com/reset-password.
CWE-644.remediation: Configure a strict ALLOWED_HOSTS whitelist and do not generate URLs solely from the Host header.

CWE-668.name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
CWE-668.description: Exposing internal debugging or administrative interfaces directly to external networks.
CWE-668.attack_vector: External attackers connecting directly to unprotected debug consoles.
CWE-668.remediation: Confine administrative endpoints behind firewalls or reverse proxies with authentication.

CWE-669.name: Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres
CWE-669.description: Leaking socket or network file descriptors into untrusted child processes via inheritance.
CWE-669.attack_vector: Child process utilizing inherited socket descriptors to communicate with internal networks.

CWE-703.name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
CWE-703.description: Silencing all exceptions with bare 'except: pass' hides critical security or database failures.
CWE-703.attack_vector: Attacker triggers an error that fails open because exception handling is completely suppressed.
CWE-703.remediation: Catch specific exception classes and log failures explicitly.

CWE-732.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CWE-732.description: Assigning overly permissive permissions (e.g. 0777 or 0666) to files allows unauthorized local users to read/modify them.
CWE-732.attack_vector: Local unprivileged users reading sensitive configs or injecting malicious code into world-writable files.
CWE-732.remediation: Use restrictive file permissions (0600 for secrets, 0640 or 0750 for group-shared resources).

CWE-754.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions in Network Stream
CWE-754.description: Reading from sockets in loops without handling EOF or connection reset conditions.
CWE-754.attack_vector: Closing connection causing server to spin in 100% CPU infinite loop reading 0 bytes.
CWE-754.remediation: Check if returned bytes are empty and break loop when connection is closed.

CWE-757.name: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation
CWE-757.description: Enabling obsolete SSL/TLS protocol versions (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1) vulnerable to downgrade attacks.
CWE-757.attack_vector: POODLE or BEAST downgrade attacks forcing insecure legacy protocol suites.
CWE-757.remediation: Configure ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT and set minimum_version to TLSv1_2 or TLSv1_3.

CWE-759.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
CWE-759.description: Hashing passwords without unique per-user cryptographic salts enables lookup table attacks.
CWE-759.attack_vector: Precomputed rainbow tables matching common unsalted password digests.
CWE-759.remediation: Always generate a cryptographically random salt (at least 16 bytes) per credential.

CWE-760.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
CWE-760.description: Employing static, hardcoded, or easily guessable salts across multiple password hashes.
CWE-760.attack_vector: Generating a single rainbow table targeted against the known static salt.
CWE-760.remediation: Generate random, unique salts per user via os.urandom(16).

CWE-770.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-770.description: Spawning unbounded threads, tasks, or worker processes on external input exhausts host memory and threads.
CWE-770.attack_vector: Flooding service with concurrent requests that cause thread or process starvation.
CWE-770.remediation: Apply concurrency limits using semaphores, bounded thread pools, and rate limiting.

CWE-775.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
CWE-775.description: Leaking socket or low-level file handles across long-running daemon lifecycles.
CWE-775.attack_vector: Denial of service via file descriptor exhaustion (EMFILE).
CWE-775.remediation: Ensure all low-level sockets and descriptors are closed in try/finally blocks.

CWE-776.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References ('Billion Laughs')
CWE-776.description: Recursively expanding nested XML entities consumes all system memory (Billion Laughs attack).
CWE-776.attack_vector: XML document with 10 levels of recursive entities expanding to gigabytes.
CWE-776.remediation: Use defusedxml, which explicitly blocks recursive entity expansion.

CWE-798.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-798.description: Hardcoding API tokens, service keys, or shared secrets directly in Python source code.
CWE-798.attack_vector: Extracting hardcoded credentials through source code access, git history, or decompiled packages.
CWE-798.remediation: Store secrets in environment variables, HashiCorp Vault, or AWS Secrets Manager.

CWE-827.name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition (DTD)
CWE-827.description: Allowing external DTDs during XML parsing enables denial of service or external entity retrieval.
CWE-827.attack_vector: External DTD references pointing to malicious remote schemas.
CWE-827.remediation: Explicitly set load_dtd=False and resolve_entities=False in XMLParser.

CWE-862.name: Missing Authorization (IDOR)
CWE-862.description: Failing to verify that an authenticated user has permission to access a specific requested object (IDOR).
CWE-862.attack_vector: Altering ID parameters in URL to access other users' private records.
CWE-862.remediation: Enforce object-level permissions by filtering queries against the current authenticated user identity.

CWE-863.name: Incorrect Authorization
CWE-863.description: Checking only if a user is logged in rather than verifying appropriate role or permission level.
CWE-863.attack_vector: Standard user accessing admin dashboard endpoints because only login status is verified.
CWE-863.remediation: Implement granular role-based or attribute-based access control (RBAC/ABAC).

CWE-915.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes ('Mass Assignment')
CWE-915.description: Binding arbitrary JSON request fields directly to object attributes allows setting is_admin or permissions.
CWE-915.attack_vector: Submitting {'is_admin': True, 'role': 'superuser'} in registration or update requests.
CWE-915.remediation: Bind request data only through strict, vetted schema fields.

CWE-916.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-916.description: Configuring password-hashing iteration counts too low, making brute-force cracking trivial.
CWE-916.attack_vector: Offline dictionary attack against low-iteration PBKDF2 or low-round bcrypt hashes.
CWE-916.remediation: Use at least 600,000 iterations for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, or work factor 12 for bcrypt.

CWE-918.name: Server-Side Request Forgery ('SSRF')
CWE-918.description: Fetching arbitrary remote URLs provided by users allows scanning internal networks and cloud metadata.
CWE-918.attack_vector: Submitting 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' to steal AWS IAM credentials.
CWE-918.remediation: Validate target URLs against an allowlist of domains, resolve IP addresses, and block private/link-local ranges.

CWE-924.name: Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission
CWE-924.description: Sending administrative control commands across TCP streams without tamper-evident signatures or encryption.
CWE-924.attack_vector: Injecting or modifying packets on unauthenticated network connections.
CWE-924.remediation: Authenticate and encrypt messages using TLS or authenticated message formats.

CWE-942.name: Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing Policy ('CORS Misconfiguration')
CWE-942.description: Configuring Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * alongside credentials allows arbitrary websites to read authenticated API responses.
CWE-942.attack_vector: Malicious site making cross-origin requests and extracting victim's confidential data.
CWE-942.remediation: Specify explicit trusted origins and avoid wildcards when credentials are supported.

CWE-943.name: NoSQL Injection
CWE-943.description: Passing unvalidated dictionary expressions or operator objects to NoSQL database queries.
CWE-943.attack_vector: Submitting JSON with $ne, $gt, or $where operators to bypass authentication or filter criteria.
CWE-943.remediation: Enforce strict schema validation and cast inputs explicitly to primitive types.

CWE-1004.name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-1004.description: Failing to set the HttpOnly flag on cookies allows client-side JavaScript to access session tokens.
CWE-1004.attack_vector: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payload reading document.cookie to hijack user accounts.
CWE-1004.remediation: Always set httponly=True on all sensitive and session cookies.

CWE-1021.name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames ('Clickjacking')
CWE-1021.description: Allowing sensitive pages to be embedded in iframes allows clickjacking attacks.
CWE-1021.attack_vector: Overlaying transparent iframes to trick users into clicking buttons.
CWE-1021.remediation: Set X-Frame-Options: DENY or Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'.

CWE-1188.name: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource
CWE-1188.description: Initializing administrative accounts or permissions with insecure default settings.
CWE-1188.attack_vector: Default accounts enabled out-of-the-box with standard credentials.
CWE-1188.remediation: Enforce safe defaults: require credentials setup on first boot and disable debug flags.

CWE-1275.name: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
CWE-1275.description: Setting SameSite=None without proper cross-origin controls leaves cookies vulnerable to CSRF.
CWE-1275.attack_vector: Third-party sites triggering cross-origin requests that automatically include authentication cookies.
CWE-1275.remediation: Set SameSite='Lax' or 'Strict' on sensitive cookies.

CWE-1327.name: Binding to All Network Interfaces
CWE-1327.description: Binding servers to 0.0.0.0 exposes internal management or debugging interfaces to all network interfaces.
CWE-1327.attack_vector: Accessing internal administrative ports from external networks.
CWE-1327.remediation: Bind development and internal services strictly to 127.0.0.1.

CWE-1333.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity ('ReDoS')
CWE-1333.description: Evaluating catastrophic backtracking regular expressions on untrusted input causes CPU exhaustion.
CWE-1333.attack_vector: Specially crafted repetitive input triggering exponential backtracking in regex engine.
CWE-1333.remediation: Avoid nested quantifiers like (a+)+, use re.escape(), or deploy linear-time regex engines.

CWE-1336.name: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
CWE-1336.description: Rendering templates from runtime-constructed strings rather than static template files.
CWE-1336.remediation: Render only trusted template files; pass user input solely as template context variables.
